title: Replying to an Invitation
short: Reply by the date asked, in the way asked; "RSVP" asks for a reply either way, and "regrets only" asks only those not coming to reply.
trouble: Learners reply "maybe," add guests who were not invited, or cancel at the last minute for a better offer. A reply is a promise.

blocks.html: An invitation ends with a request: reply. RSVP comes from the French répondez s'il vous plaît, "please reply." It is one of the clearest rules in etiquette, and one of the most often broken.
Reply by the date asked, in the way asked. "RSVP" asks for a reply either way, yes or no. "Regrets only" asks only those who are not coming to reply.

The host is planning food, chairs and space around your answer. A prompt reply lets them plan; silence leaves them guessing and chasing guests. Once you say yes, the host counts on you, so a reply is a promise: cancel only for a real reason, and as early as you can.

head: The invitation says
You are coming
You are not coming
blocks.cap: What each request asks of you.

messages.text: We'd love to have you for dinner on the 9th! RSVP by the 2nd?

choices.text: Maybe! I'll see how the week goes.
choices.why: A "maybe" leaves the host unable to plan.

choices.text: Thank you so much! I'd love to come. See you on the 9th.
choices.why: A clear, warm yes, sent promptly.

choices.text: Can I bring my roommate and her brother?
choices.why: Don't add guests to an invitation; the host invited whom they could.

blocks.title: Regrets only
blocks.q: Hana's office party invitation says "Regrets only." She plans to go. What should she do?
steps: "Regrets only" means reply only if you are not coming.
She is coming, so no reply is needed. She simply shows up on time.
blocks.a: Nothing: no reply needed when you are coming.

blocks.title: A better offer
blocks.q: Omar said yes to Kofi's dinner on Saturday. On Thursday, he is invited to a concert the same night. What should he do?
steps: His yes was a promise, and Kofi has planned food for him.
He keeps the dinner date and declines the concert kindly.
Canceling for a better offer tells the host they were a placeholder.

blocks.html: Replying "maybe," adding guests who were not invited, or canceling at the last minute for a better offer. A reply is a promise. Quick check: if everyone replied the way you did, could the host plan the party?

sources.name: Present-day American custom, as etiquette writers widely describe it: RSVP and regrets only
Emily Post, Etiquette in Society, in Business, in Politics and at Home (1922; public domain), its chapter on invitations, acceptances and regrets (history only: many details have changed)
